step1_figure.description: Figure 20.13 illustrates two complementary MOSFET-only self-biasing circuits: one where an NMOS device acts as a long-channel resistor to set the bias current mirrored by PMOS transistor M4 (top), and one where a PMOS device acts as a long-channel resistor to set the bias current mirrored by NMOS transistor M2 (bottom).

i_op.description: Output current of the MOSFET-only bias circuit using an NMOS transistor as a resistor (mirrored through M4P)

equation.formula: I_op = ((VDD - VTHN - VTHP) / (sqrt(2*L3/(KPp*W3)) + sqrt(2*L1/(KPn*W1))))^2 * (1 + lambda * VDD) / (1 + lambda * VSD3)
equation.explanation: Calculates the reference current established across the diode-connected PMOS M3 and NMOS resistor M1, mirrored to output transistor M4 with channel-length modulation correction.
equation.assumptions: Square-law saturation operation for both M1 and M3, neglecting higher-order short-channel velocity saturation effects.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Device threshold tolerances and mobility degradation shift output current around the nominal 4.15 uA value.

i_on.description: Output current of the MOSFET-only bias circuit using a PMOS transistor as a resistor (mirrored through M2N)

equation.formula: I_on = ((VDD - VTHN - VTHP) / (sqrt(2*L3/(KPp*W3)) + sqrt(2*L1/(KPn*W1))))^2 * (1 + lambda * VDD) / (1 + lambda * VDS1)
equation.explanation: Calculates the reference current generated across PMOS resistor M3 and diode-connected NMOS M1, mirrored to output transistor M2.
equation.assumptions: Square-law saturation model for both M1 and M3, identical threshold magnitudes.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Output current is determined primarily by PMOS resistor dimensions and saturation conditions.

di_op_dvdd.description: Sensitivity of I_op with respect to power supply voltage changes (dI_op/dVDD)

equation.explanation: Represents how quickly the reference current in the NMOS-as-resistor topology changes when VDD fluctuates.
equation.assumptions: Long-channel model sensitivity neglecting channel length modulation contribution to dI/dVDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: With K = 2.489e5 V^2/A and (VDD - VTHN - VTHP) = 0.96 V: dI_op/dVDD = 2 * 0.96 / 2.489e5 = 7.71 uA/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite output conductance increases sensitivity above the ideal square-law derivative.

di_on_dvdd.description: Sensitivity of I_on with respect to power supply voltage changes (dI_on/dVDD)

equation.explanation: Quantifies the variation of the PMOS-as-resistor circuit's mirrored current with power supply voltage.
equation.assumptions: Neglecting body effect and second-order modulation.

sky130_expected.calculation: With K = 4.077e5 V^2/A and (VDD - VTHN - VTHP) = 0.96 V: dI_on/dVDD = 2 * 0.96 / 4.077e5 = 4.71 uA/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher resistance factor K leads to a lower sensitivity compared to the NMOS-resistor topology.

v_bias_nmos_res.description: Bias gate voltage at node N001 in the NMOS-as-resistor circuit

equation.explanation: Sets the operating gate-to-source bias for NMOS device M1 which drops the bulk of VDD as an active resistor.
equation.assumptions: M1 is in saturation with source tied to 0V.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Since M1 acts as the resistor with large L (270u), it drops most of VDD (~1.28V) while M3 drops ~0.52V.

v_bias_pmos_res.description: Bias gate voltage at node N002 in the PMOS-as-resistor circuit

equation.explanation: Sets the operating gate-to-source bias for NMOS device M1 when PMOS M3 acts as the long resistor.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Since PMOS M3 drops most of VDD (~1.32V), NMOS M1 has low VGS (~0.48V).

step3_testbench.description: DC sweep testbench measuring output currents I_op and I_on, gate bias voltages V(N001) and V(N002), and sensitivities dI_op/dVDD and dI_on/dVDD over supply variations.
